extracted.intended_audience: tribal leaders and their designees, federal agency staff who organize consultations, and members of the public tracking tribal consultation notices
extracted.subtask_description: Search-results/index page listing federal tribal consultation notices and excerpts that state procedural standards for how agencies solicit, conduct, and record Tribal consultation (e.g., who may participate, how to submit comments, legal/policy authorities). Useful for preparing to participate or for agencies drafting consultation notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with Executive Order 13175 and agency consultation policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Consultations are held to conform to the requirements of Executive Order 13175 (Consultation and Coordination With Indian Tribal Governments) and each agency's Tribal Consultation Policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notices state that the purpose of meetings is to conform to E.O. 13175 and agency tribal consultation policies (e.g., "The purpose of this tribal consultation meeting is to conform to the requirements of Executive Order 13175"). Agencies reference their own policies/links and frame consultations as a required component of deliberations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government-to-government consultation scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Tribal consultation applies to Department/agency actions that affect federally recognized Indian Tribes and requires government-to-government engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy language: consultation "applies to any Department action that affects federally recognized Indian Tribes" and requires that the Department's government-to-government consultation involve appropriate Tribal and Departmental Officials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may participate (federally recognized tribal leaders, designees, proxies)
rubrics_metrics.description: Participation is limited to tribal governments' leaders, their designated representatives, proxies, or invited tribal citizens; agencies often require notification if a proxy will attend.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notices repeatedly state attendees should be "leaders of tribal governments and their designated representatives" or "leaders or their proxies," and place limits (e.g., "open to citizens of federally and State recognized Tribes by invitation"). Some notices require notification of proxies by a given deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invitation-only or limited-access participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Some consultations are explicitly limited in attendance (e.g., only tribal representatives and agency staff), not open to press or the general public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: "open only to leaders of federally recognized Tribal Nations and their proxies. It is not open to the press or members of the public." FERC/Idaho Power notices state intervenors may attend but participation limited to tribal representatives and staff; non-tribal attendees may be excused during sensitive disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solicitation of written comments and comment deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies solicit written comments as part of the consultation process and set explicit deadlines for receipt of those comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notices instruct where and by when to submit comments (e.g., "Any questions or topics to be considered in the Tribal consultation meetings must be received in writing via email by [date]"). Comments often become part of the administrative record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-registration and registration mechanics
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies require or request pre-registration for virtual/in-person consultation sessions, providing registration links or email addresses and deadlines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: registration via Zoom link or WebEx platform; pre-registration deadlines given ("pre-registration deadline date is [date]"). Notices give specific instructions (e.g., use a particular subject line or send to a named email).

rubrics_metrics.name: Virtual and in-person modalities specified (platforms, access)
rubrics_metrics.description: Notices specify whether consultation is virtual or in-person and often name the platform (Zoom, ZoomGov, WebEx) or physical location and logistical details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: "virtually through Zoom," "meetings will be held virtually on the WebEx platform," or physical venue addresses and times. Links and registration instructions accompany virtual sessions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agenda content tied to statutory/policy purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: Agendas are expected to reflect the statutory purposes of tribal consultations and focus on topics that affect tribal communities (funding allocations, program standards, proposed rules, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notices mention purpose topics: "discuss ways to better meet the needs of American Indian and Alaska Native (AIAN) children," "review and promulgation of Head Start Program Performance Standards," or comment on proposed rulemakings (HIPAA changes, HUBZone reforms).

rubrics_metrics.name: Testimony and comments become part of the administrative record
rubrics_metrics.description: Oral testimony and submitted comments during consultations will be incorporated into the administrative record for agency decisionmaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit language: "Testimony presented at this Tribal consultation will become part of the administrative record for [Agency]’s consideration when the Agency deliberates" and "FHWA and TxDOT will consider the comments submitted when making its decision."

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential handling of sensitive cultural/archaeological information
rubrics_metrics.description: Consultations include procedures to protect sensitive Tribal information; non-tribal attendees may be excused when location-specific cultural/archaeological information is disclosed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: "If Tribal representatives decide to disclose information about a specific location which could create a risk or harm to an archaeological site or Native American cultural resource, attendees other than Tribal representatives and Commission staff will be excused for that portion of the meeting."

rubrics_metrics.name: Agencies will highlight progress and follow up on prior concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: Consultations include review of progress made in addressing issues raised in prior consultations and provide continuity across sessions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notices state: "OHS will also highlight the progress made in addressing issues and concerns raised in the previous OHS Tribal Consultations" and may provide summaries or follow-up opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agencies may hold pre-consultation webinars to prepare tribes
rubrics_metrics.description: Some agencies offer optional pre-consultation webinars to overview programs and help tribal participants prepare substantive feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: DOL's optional pre-consultation webinar "will offer Tribal Nation leaders or their proxies an overview of OA and OWI programming, as well as time to answer technical questions . . . to help prepare for a substantive discussion."

rubrics_metrics.name: Deference to tribal officials for formal comment and allowance for expert staff
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies will defer to tribal officials for formal comment and tribes may include or confer with expert staff during consultations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notices reflect commenters' requests: option for authorized proxies to speak; ability for tribal leaders to include and confer with their expert staff during consultations; agencies note they value tribal leader input and may accommodate these requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific question prompts and requests for recommendations/best practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Notices often include explicit questions or topic prompts to guide requested feedback (recommendations for policy, best practices, updates to consultation policies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: NEA asks, "What recommendations do you have regarding the NEA's Tribal Consultation Policy?" SBA requests "comments and input on best practices for how entity-owned firms market their capabilities" and other targeted questions to solicit useful feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time-limited comment periods tied to meetings
rubrics_metrics.description: Official comment periods are time-limited and may remain open for a set number of days after the in-person/virtual consultation session.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: "The official comment period for this consultation will remain open for 30 days after the in-person consultation session occurs." Notices list dates and cutoffs for written submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultation outcomes may inform rulemaking and policy reform
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies state that consultation input will inform potential rulemakings, proposed regulatory revisions, MOUs, and implementation of Executive Orders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notices indicate consultation feedback "will become part of the administrative record" and will be considered when deliberating changes (e.g., HUBZone program revisions, WIPO Treaty decisions, MOU renewals).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope inclusions (which Tribes and communities are covered)
rubrics_metrics.description: Notices clarify which groups are included (federally recognized Tribal Nations, State-recognized Tribes, Native Hawaiians, other Pacific Islanders) when soliciting input.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: USPTO notice clarifies: 'For purposes of this Notice, the words "Tribe" or "Tribes" are intended to refer to Tribal Nations, State recognized Tribes, other Tribes, and Native Hawaiians and other Pacific Islanders.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural notices correcting or clarifying prior consultation statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies issue corrections when prior notices contained incorrect statements about ongoing consultation or requests for formal consultation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: A correction notice clarifies that FHWA and TxDOT "have not received such requests and there is no active, ongoing consultation with Tribes," and explains how comments will be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agencies may limit participation or participation scope in matters uniquely affecting Tribes
rubrics_metrics.description: When rulemakings or proceedings uniquely affect Tribes, agencies will conduct Tribal consultation specifically and may limit or structure participation accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: FERC will conduct Tribal consultation per its Policy Statement on Consultation when a petition seeks a rulemaking that "involves issues that would uniquely affect Tribes." Notices may announce consultations 'because the petition seeks to have the Commission institute a rulemaking proceeding that involves issues that would uniquely affect Tribes.'
